finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /profile/avatar fetches an attacker-supplied URL server-side. The only validation is a string prefix check for 'https://'. There is no host or IP allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local block, and no DNS pinning. axios follows redirects by default (follow-redirects, up to 5), and its redirect handling permits https->http downgrade. An attacker can point at an https URL they control that 302s to http://169.254.169.254/ (cloud metadata) or http://users.internal:8080/. They can also use https URLs directly against internal hosts or ports with TLS, or a hostname that resolves to a private IP (DNS rebinding). Response data is not returned, but the bytes length is, and status/timing differences give a blind-SSRF oracle. Internal requests are sent with GET to arbitrary internal endpoints.

trace.note: Route handler POST /profile/avatar, no auth middleware
url = req.body.avatarUrl taken directly from the request
Only check: typeof string and startsWith('https://'). It is a string check, not a parsed-host check.
axios.get(url) with default redirect following and no host/IP restrictions or timeout
Response size is reflected to the caller, giving a side-channel

finding.guards_checked: Checked the startsWith('https://') scheme check: it does not stop redirects to http:// or internal https hosts. Checked for a host allowlist, IP/metadata blocking, maxRedirects=0, a custom agent or lookup for DNS pinning, and auth middleware (app.use only has express.json()). None exist. The second axios call at server.js:20 uses a constant base URL with encodeURIComponent(id), so it is not an SSRF sink (at most path-level traversal on the fixed host) and I excluded it.

verdict.guard_found: none (only typeof string and startsWith('https://') at server.js:11, a scheme-prefix check; no host allowlist, IP blocking, maxRedirects, or auth middleware)
verdict.reason: server.js:10 takes req.body.avatarUrl unauthenticated, server.js:11 only checks the 'https://' prefix, and server.js:14 calls axios.get(url) with default redirect following and no host/IP restrictions, with the response size returned at server.js:15.
